game: CHI@DET Week 2 2025, kickoff 2025-09-14 13:00 ET, DET -6, total 46.5, roof dome

script.base: Detroit leads by the half in a dome game the book prices at about 26-20. Chicago, a 6-point dog that posted -0.43 EPA per dropback against the blitz, faces a 43% blitz and cannot lean on D'Andre Swift against a front that allowed 3.29 YPC and two 10-plus runs, so Caleb Williams is forced into quick throws while Detroit hands David Montgomery the late carries.
script.flip1: Chicago hangs around or leads, Williams avoids the blitz, and DJ Moore's week-1 deep profile (5 targets, 94 air yards, 57 yards) turns this into a shootout: Detroit cannot sit on the run, Montgomery's carry spike never comes, and Swift keeps a 15-plus carry day.
script.flip2: Detroit is up big early. Montgomery's carries rise until garbage time, Swift's rushing line dies, and if the lead gets out of hand Detroit's skill starters lose late snaps. A true blowout is the lesser flip at only -6.

injury_fallout: Known pre-kick from the nflverse injury report, not inactives (90-minute checkpoint not in the pack). CHI CB Kyler Gordon is Out (hamstring), so slot, TE and RB receiving on Detroit's side (Sam LaPorta, Jahmyr Gibbs as a receiver) face a backup; that is not yet in any reprice. CHI DT Grady Jarrett is Questionable (knee): if he sits, a run defense that already allowed 4.62 YPC gets softer for Montgomery and Gibbs. CHI WR Jahdae Walker is Doubtful and was not a week-1 target factor. DET LB Trevor Nowaske is Out (elbow), which helps Chicago's middle (Cole Kmet, Colston Loveland, Swift catches) against a defense that already allowed 15.5 YPA on 8 middle throws. DET S Kerby Joseph is Questionable (knee); if he sits, Moore and Rome Odunze's deep air yards get a coverage break. DET T Taylor Decker is Questionable (shoulder); if he sits, Detroit's already-poor week-1 rush efficiency (Montgomery 2.3 YPC, Gibbs 2.1) can stay broken and quick throws to Gibbs and LaPorta rise. DET RB Sione Vaki is Doubtful and had no listed week-1 carries, so he does not change the Gibbs/Montgomery split.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Proxy is location YPA: Detroit allowed 15.5 YPA on 8 middle throws versus 4.44 left (9) and 4.8 right (5), so they bottle the outside and bleed the middle. Chicago allowed 7.75 left (8), 8.5 middle (2) and 6.4 right (10), a small middle sample and no shell read.
matchup.pressure: Detroit blitzed 43%. Chicago's only dropback split is -0.43 EPA vs blitz and +0.21 vs no blitz, so pressure should kill deep WR yards (Moore 94 air yards, Odunze 55, Olamide Zaccheaus 59) and push checkdowns to Swift and the TEs. Chicago blitzed only 21%. Detroit was +0.49 EPA vs blitz and -0.03 vs none, so Chicago's low blitz rate does not hand Detroit the blitz boost from week 1.
matchup.bleeds: Detroit run defense is the stingy unit: 3.29 YPC, two runs of 10-plus, and only 3 of 22 passes of 20-plus, with the bleed isolated to the middle. Chicago run defense is the soft unit: 4.62 YPC and four runs of 10-plus, plus a modest 2 of 23 passes of 20-plus. Gordon out is the coverage hole; Nowaske out widens the middle for Chicago.
matchup.overlap: The clean bettable overlap is Chicago's soft run front versus Detroit's early-down back in a lead script, not a WR-versus-corner chart (none saved). The receiving overlap (LaPorta 9 targets/79 yards and Gibbs 10 targets into a Gordon-less slot and a middle that allowed 15.5 YPA) is real, but those stand-in lines sit on the week-1 outputs, so they are not the two legs. Chicago's top outside shots (Moore, Odunze) attack the part of Detroit that held up (outside YPA 4.4-4.8) while Caleb is bad against the blitz.

form: One 2025 game only, so there is no 3-4 game trend. Chicago rush: Swift 17/53, Williams 6/58, Moore 3/8. Chicago targets: Odunze 9/37 on 55 air, Zaccheaus 7/42 on 59 air, Moore 5/57 on 94 air (explosive, low volume), Swift 5/12 on -3 air, Kmet 4/31, Loveland 2/12. Detroit rush was a clunker for both backs: Montgomery 11/25, Gibbs 9/19. Detroit targets: Gibbs 10/31 on 0 air, LaPorta 9/79 on 45 air, St. Brown only 6/45 on 53 air, Jameson Williams 5/23 on 26 air, Montgomery 4/18. Moore's 57 yards and LaPorta's 79 are the fluky-efficiency flags; Swift's 53 and Montgomery's 25 sit on the stand-in lines. Kyle Monangai is not in the rusher list (0 rush yards).

pro_edge.script_read: Spread is 6, so the 3.5-plus dog-throws rule applies: Chicago WR/TE/RB targets up, Detroit lead-back carries up late. Total 46.5 is not a slog and not a shootout lock. Not a blowout flag for automatic starter-sit; late-snap risk only if flip 2 hits. Volume should be built off shares, not the one-game averages.
pro_edge.best_price: No two-sided price saved on any listed prop. Anchor no-vig N/A. No Pinnacle, Circa or BetOnline number to beat. Power devig cannot be shown. No alt prices.
pro_edge.lagging: Every main line in the pack is a stand-in equal to the single 2025 game (Swift rush 53.5 on 53, Montgomery rush 25.5 on 25, Gibbs rush+rec 50.5 on 50, LaPorta 79.5 on 79, Moore 57.5 on 57). No saved move after the spread or total. Lines have not been repriced for Chicago's 4.62 YPC, Detroit's 3.29 YPC, the 43% blitz, or Gordon/Nowaske being out.
pro_edge.sleepers: Out: Kyler Gordon (CHI CB) — same-position receiving lines for LaPorta, Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown are unmoved at week-1 yards. Out: Trevor Nowaske (DET LB) — Swift/Kmet/Loveland middle lines unmoved. Doubtful, not a role change: Sione Vaki (DET RB depth), Jahdae Walker (CHI WR depth). Questionable, not a sleeper until ruled out: Grady Jarrett, Taylor Decker, Kerby Joseph. No IR note.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Montgomery's 25.5 rushing line is pinned to an 11-carry, 2.3-YPC week-1 clunker, and Chicago just allowed 4.62 YPC with four runs of 10-plus, so a Detroit lead should give the early-down back both better efficiency and the late carries.
edge_players.must_be_true: He keeps the early-down share he had in week 1 (11 carries to Gibbs's 9), Detroit is not chasing, and Decker either plays or the line is not the whole reason for the 2.3 YPC.
edge_players.kills_it: Decker sits and both backs stay near 2 YPC, Gibbs steals the rushing work, or Chicago leads and Detroit abandons the run.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Swift needs another 17-carry, 53-yard day to clear 53.5, but Detroit allowed 3.29 YPC and only two 10-plus runs, and Chicago as a 6-point dog that was bad against a 43% blitz is the side that falls behind and abandons the run.
edge_players.must_be_true: Detroit leads or at least keeps Chicago in passing mode, the week-1 Detroit run defense is not a one-game mirage, and Williams's 6/58 scrambles do not come with a full Swift carry count.
edge_players.kills_it: Chicago stays close or leads (flip 1) and Swift holds 16-17 carries, or he breaks the two-run explosive cap Detroit showed in one game. A trailing-script checkdown spike does not kill a rush-yards under.

data_check.notes: No projection, no sims, no Pinnacle or Circa no-vig. Every prop is 'no price' and the rung equals the only 2025 game, so there is no independent number that agrees or beats a fair price by 3 points. model_p 0.56 and 0.55 are hand reads, not sim outputs, and must not pass the edge gate or be sized. Form sits on both lines (disagree-by-absence, not a second sample against the read). Decker and Jarrett are unresolved. Per the rules this flags both leans for a human; it does not cut them, and it does not upgrade them. Anything at 70% would be untrustworthy anyway; these are not that.

market_rung_price: Main rungs only, no alt, no saved price: David Montgomery rushyds over 25.5; D'Andre Swift rushyds under 53.5. Nothing to shop. Short alts are out. Stake proposal withheld until a no-vig exists and a real model beats it by 3 or more. Left off on purpose: LaPorta recyds 79.5 (week-1 ceiling, Gordon-out overlap but no price), Gibbs rushrecyds 50.5 (same Detroit run story, shares carries, 10-target week can regress), Moore recyds under 57.5 (blitz plus outside YPA, but one bomb kills it).
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Montgomery stayed at 8 carries and 2.3 YPC because Decker's shoulder was the week-1 problem, not the opponent, Gibbs took the closer work, and Chicago's 4.62 YPC was one soft game with Jarrett still on the field. Swift went over 53.5 because the game stayed inside one score, he got another 16-17 carries, and Detroit's 3.29 YPC did not travel. That counter is strong enough to keep both at lean and flagged, not strong enough to erase the matchup gap written above.
slip_story: One story only: Detroit leads and runs the clock, Chicago trails and cannot run. Stack is Montgomery rush over with Swift rush under. Do not add Chicago WR overs, a game over, or LaPorta/Gibbs receiving overs that need a pass-volume shootout. Gibbs rush over 19.5 would fit the same run story but is the third name and cannibalizes Montgomery's carries, so he stays off a 2-leg card. No TDs, no receptions, no passing yards.
